chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

A man does not testify against another man with disbelief at all, except that one of the two will be returned with it: if he testified against a disbeliever, it was true; and if he testified against a believer, the disbelief returns upon him. Beware of reviling the believers.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of testifying against a believer with disbelief?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'return of the charge' (i'rad al-dhamir), where the accuser bears the spiritual consequence of their testimony if it proves inaccurate. It highlights the high status of the believer, such that falsely attributing kufr to them results in the accuser acquiring that very attribute, serving as a stern warning against hasty judgment and reviling (ta'tib) the faithful. This concept is central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of testimony and the preservation of communal honor.
